resources.name: Nutanix Prism Central
resources.summary: Control plane for clusters, VMs, storage, and networking. Use cases read inventory and metrics from it; write operations require review.

env.name: PRISM_CENTRAL_ENDPOINT
env.description: Base URL of the Prism Central v4 API, including port.

env.name: PRISM_CENTRAL_USERNAME
env.description: Service account with the least privilege the use case needs.

env.name: PRISM_CENTRAL_PASSWORD
env.description: Service account password. Never commit; sourced from a Kubernetes Secret in cluster.

env.name: PRISM_CENTRAL_INSECURE_TLS
env.description: Set to true only for lab endpoints using self-signed certificates.

resources.name: Nutanix Kubernetes Platform
resources.summary: Managed Kubernetes that hosts the portal and any use-case backends. Also the target for GPU workloads scheduled by use cases.

env.name: NKP_CLUSTER_NAME
env.description: Name of the workload cluster the portal is deployed to.

env.name: NKP_API_SERVER
env.description: Kubernetes API server URL for the workload cluster.

env.name: NKP_NAMESPACE
env.description: Namespace that owns the portal and its use-case backends.

env.name: NKP_KUBECONFIG
env.description: Path to a kubeconfig. Omit in cluster, where the mounted service account is used instead.

resources.name: Nutanix Enterprise AI
resources.summary: On-premises OpenAI-compatible inference endpoint. Not reachable from the NKP cluster and publishes no embedding model, so the backends target the OpenRouter gateway instead. Retained for workstation use and for when cluster egress is opened.

env.name: NAI_ENDPOINT
env.description: OpenAI-compatible base URL. Call over plain HTTP so the reasoning field is not discarded.

env.name: NAI_API_KEY
env.description: API key issued per use case so usage can be attributed and revoked independently.

env.name: NAI_CHAT_MODEL
env.description: Default chat/completion model name as published by the endpoint.

env.name: NAI_EMBEDDING_MODEL
env.description: Embedding model. This endpoint publishes none yet; must match the model that populated the vector collection.

resources.name: OpenRouter Model Gateway
resources.summary: OpenAI-compatible gateway serving NVIDIA Nemotron chat, embedding, and rerank models. Reachable from the NKP cluster, unlike the on-premises Enterprise AI endpoint, so it is the gateway the backends target.

env.name: OPENROUTER_BASE_URL
env.description: OpenAI-compatible base URL. Also serves /embeddings and a non-standard /rerank.

env.name: OPENROUTER_API_KEY
env.description: Account-wide key. Free-variant rate limits apply per account, not per key, so issuing one key per use case does not raise the ceiling.

env.name: OPENROUTER_CHAT_MODEL
env.description: Default chat model. Returns a separate reasoning field whose tokens count against max_tokens.

env.name: OPENROUTER_CHAT_MODEL_FAST
env.description: Lower-latency alternative for short narrative. Also accepts audio, image, and video input.

env.name: OPENROUTER_EMBEDDING_MODEL
env.description: Embedding model. Free variant only; there is no paid variant to fall back to.

env.name: OPENROUTER_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS
env.description: Fixed at 2048. The model rejects any other value, and 2048 exceeds pgvector's 2000-dimension index limit — see the vector database README.

env.name: OPENROUTER_RERANK_MODEL
env.description: Second-stage reranker over vector-search candidates. Scores are relative, not calibrated probabilities.

env.name: OPENROUTER_MAX_TOKENS
env.description: Budget generously: reasoning tokens are billed against this, and a tight budget truncates the answer before any content is emitted.

resources.name: Casino Data Platform
resources.summary: One Postgres holding the simulated CMS (cms_raw), the shared contracts (analytics.player_scores, analytics.eligible_players, analytics.decision_log), and a private schema per use case. The schema is the contract; no code is shared.

env.name: CASINO_DB_HOST
env.description: Postgres service address. Prefer the in-cluster name.

env.name: CASINO_DB_PORT
env.description: Postgres port.

env.name: CASINO_DB_NAME
env.description: Database holding cms_raw, analytics, and the uc_* schemas.

env.name: CASINO_DB_USER
env.description: Role issued per use case. Read on cms_raw, write only on its own schema and the contract columns it owns.

env.name: CASINO_DB_PASSWORD
env.description: Role password. Sourced from a Kubernetes Secret in cluster.

env.name: CASINO_DB_SSLMODE
env.description: Set to disable only for in-cluster lab traffic.

resources.name: Model Registry
resources.summary: MLflow tracking and registry on NKP. The run id it issues is the model_version written to player_scores and decision_log, which is what makes a recommendation reconstructible at audit.

env.name: MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI
env.description: Tracking server URL. Training jobs log runs here; scoring jobs resolve model versions from it.

env.name: MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_PREFIX
env.description: Prefix for experiment names so use cases do not collide in the registry.

env.name: MLFLOW_TRACKING_TOKEN
env.description: Bearer token, if the tracking server enforces authentication.

resources.name: Vector Database
resources.summary: Retrieval store, pgvector inside the casino Postgres. Now usable: the OpenRouter gateway serves embeddings. Vectors are 2048-dimensional, which exceeds pgvector's 2000-dimension index limit, so indexes are built on a halfvec cast.

env.name: VECTOR_DB_KIND
env.description: One of pgvector, milvus, qdrant, or weaviate. Drives which client a use case vendors in.

env.name: VECTOR_DB_ENDPOINT
env.description: Connection URL. Prefer the in-cluster service address.

env.name: VECTOR_DB_API_KEY
env.description: Token or user:password pair, if the deployment enforces authentication.

env.name: VECTOR_DB_DATABASE
env.description: Logical database. Collections are namespaced per use case beneath it.
